newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa says Europe restructuring to continue.
newsitem.headline: Dasa says Europe restructuring to continue.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) said on Monday the restructuring of Europe's aerospace industry would continue despite France's decision to halt the privatisation of Thomson-CSF.
"The process of restructuring in Europe is not dependent on Thomson. We do not see it as endangered," Dasa spokesman Andreas Breitsprecher told Reuters.

Breitsprecher added that Dasa had no position on the move by the French Socialist government. "We are not taking a position. We must wait to see what are the concrete intentions of the French government. They have not disclosed that yet."
Prime Minster Lionel Jospin on Friday announced France would suspend the sale of its 58 percent share of Thomson-CSF, a maker of radars and other defence electronics.

Paris said it would issue new guidelines for promoting European defence cooperation, but also said it intended to use Thomson-CSF to create "a French professional and defence electronics pillar with a decisive public shareholding."
Dasa was supporting French conglomerate Lagardere Groupe in bidding for the 58 percent stake. Alcatel Alsthom had also submitted a bid.

A unit of car maker Daimler-Benz AG, Dasa has called for consolidating European manufacturers into a single aerospace group able to stand up to the mounting competitive might of American companies like Boeing Co.
Even if Thomson becomes part of a French defence group, Europe's aerospace industry could still consolidate around the Airbus commercial airliner consortium, Breitsprecher said.
"Thomson is not the only cornerstone for restructuring," he said.
